A former Bangladesh Air Force officer, KM Tahsif Souri, was found dead in a river in Dhaka on Thursday, a day after he went missing.According to the Daily Star, the 28-year-old had reportedly recorded a video showing former prime minister Sheikh Hasina leaving Bangladesh on August 5, 2024,River police recovered Souri's body from the Tongi Bandar Ghat area after receiving a call through the national emergency helpline 999.The body was taken to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital for an autopsy. His identity was confirmed after his mobile phone and wristwatch were found with the body.According to Prothom Alo, Souri lived with his family in Sector 18 of Uttara.Police said the cause of death was not yet known. Although drowning was suspected, officials said the postmortem report would help establish the cause.Souri's father KM Enayetul Karim Helal said he did not know who was responsible for his son's death. He told Jago News that Souri had sometimes expressed fears about his safety.“Tahsif would sometimes tell me that he was feeling a little apprehensive. But he never told me what he was worried about,” Helal said.According to his father, Souri was dismissed from the Air Force on disciplinary grounds. He later worked at the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB), Netra News and, most recently, Virgo Tobacco.“Before evening, one of his junior friends came to call him from downstairs.Tahsif told his mother, ‘Dip is here. I’ll go and talk to him.’ He went downstairs but never returned home,” he said.Souri's reported role in recording the video has drawn attention to his death. Hasina fled Dhaka on August 5, 2024, as mass protests led to the collapse of her government.She reportedly left by military helicopter before boarding a Bangladesh Air Force C-130J Hercules aircraft that flew to India's Hindon airbase in Ghaziabad.Hasina has remained in exile in India and has vowed to return to Bangladesh. However, police have not established any link between Souri's death and the video he reportedly recorded.
Article Summary: KM Tahsif Souri was found dead in a river in Dhaka on Thursday. The 28-year-old had reportedly recorded a video showing former prime minister Sheikh Hasina leaving Bangladesh on August 5, 2024. Police have not established any link between Souri's death and the video.

Article Title: Bangladesh: Hindu salon owner stabbed to death over unpaid haircut bills; one arrested
Article Text: Days after a Hindu schoolteacher was beaten to death in a land dispute, another Hindu man has been killed in Bangladesh. A 43-year-old salon owner was allegedly stabbed to death following a dispute over payment for haircuts in Mymensingh district. Police have arrested a 28-year-old man in connection with the killing.According to Bangladeshi media outlet Prothom Alo, at least 10 stab wounds were found on Rishi’s throat, larynx, chest, back and hands. The incident occurred in the Jamirdia area of Bhaluka upazila on Tuesday evening, according to local media reports.The deceased, identified as Rabindra Rishi, owned Apurba Hair Cutting salon at Muktijoddha Market in Bhaluka. Prothom Alo reported that the accused, Saddam Hossain, allegedly attacked Rishi with a sharp weapon after a dispute over unpaid bills and his refusal to provide haircuts on credit.Rishi’s wife, Suchitra Rani Rishi, told local media that Hossain frequently took money from her husband for drugs and did not pay for haircuts. She said the two had argued over the unpaid amounts and that Hossain had threatened to kill her husband a few days before the incident.According to the murder complaint filed by Rishi’s mother, Sulak Rani Rishi, at Bhaluka Model Police Station, the attack took place at around 5.30 pm (local time). Rishi was sitting inside his salon and talking to his brother, Manik Rishi, when Hossain allegedly entered with a sharp knife and stabbed him repeatedly in the neck.The complaint states that Rishi attempted to escape to a nearby shop, where he was stabbed in the chest. He then sought refuge in the courtyard of a nearby house, where the accused allegedly knocked him to the ground and stabbed him in the chest, back and hand. Rishi died from his injuries.Police arrested Hossain and produced him before a court, which sent him to jail. The court scheduled November 1 for a hearing on the police request for five days of remand to question the accused. The investigation is ongoing.The killing comes days after another Hindu man, 55-year-old schoolteacher Manoranjan Roy, was reportedly beaten to death during an arbitration meeting over a land dispute in Dinajpur district. Police said Roy had attempted to mediate between the parties and calm tensions before he was killed.
Article Summary: Rabindra Rishi, 43, was allegedly stabbed to death in Mymensingh district. Police have arrested a 28-year-old man in connection with the killing. Rishi's wife told local media that the two had argued over the unpaid amounts.

Article Title: JeI functionary met Indian intel official in secret: Bangladesh PM aide
Article Text:
File photo: Supporters of Bangladesh's Jamaat-e-Islami and its allies chant slogans during a protest against post-election violence in Dhaka, Bangladesh

DHAKA: Days after Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman claimed attempts were being made to destablise the country, his special assistant Md Rashed Khan has alleged a senior functionary of Bangladesh’s largest opposition party Jamaat-e-Islami had a secret meeting with a senior Indian intelligence official.Targetting JeI secretary general Mia Golam Parwar, Rashed, in a Facebook post Tuesday, said, “If Golam Parwar believes in ethical politics, I hope he will clarify the matter of this secret meeting. Otherwise, it will be assumed that Jamaat has become involved in a deep conspiracy against the state. The first trap in this conspiracy is a plan for Jamaat to launch a movement alongside Awami League!” In response, hardline JeI said it doubted the mental and political well-being of those spreading such false information and challenged them to prove their allegation. Rashed questioned why people who speak against India throughout the day would take part in a secret meeting with an Indian intelligence official. “Meeting an Indian diplomat and meeting a senior Indian intelligence official are not the same thing,” he wrote.Rejecting the allegation, JeI said it conducts its political activities through constitutional and systematic means and maintains diplomatic relations with foreign countries.
Article Summary: Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman claimed attempts were being made to destablise the country. His special assistant Md Rashed Khan has alleged a senior functionary of Bangladesh’s largest opposition party Jamaat-e-Islami had a secret meeting with a senior Indian intelligence official.
